newsitem.title: FRANCE: French public sector unions call Oct 17 strike.
newsitem.headline: French public sector unions call Oct 17 strike.

text.p: France's largest public sector unions appealed on Monday for some four million state workers to strike for 24 hours on October 17 to press for wage increases and protest against government plans to reduce state payrolls.
"We are going to do all we can to make sure it succeeds," Philippe Antoine, deputy director of the federation of civil service workers at the giant CFDT union, told Reuters.
Union officials said the appeal for a "national day of action, strikes and protests" would hit all public sector functions including hospitals, state agencies, and local governments.
The principal unions in France's civil service are seeking the immediate opening of wage talks with the government despite Prime Minister Alain Juppe's freeze on wage increases this year.

Juppe's budget plans for next year including trimming civil service numbers by 6,500 to 7,000 workers. Though this would be accomplished primarily by erosion rather than lay-offs, unions fear this is only a start.

While unions have been warning of trouble during the year's final months, most analysts still believe prospects are remote of strikes on the scale of the crippling stoppages that paralysed much of France last November and December.
